sections.content:
Mastering the subjunctive at B1 requires choosing between current/future actions vs completed past actions:

• **Present Subjunctive** (*hables, vengas*): Refers to simultaneous or future events:
  *Espero que vengas a mi fiesta mañana.* (I hope you come tomorrow.)
• **Present Perfect Subjunctive** (*hayas hablado, hayas venido*): Refers to completed events:
  *Espero que hayas venido en metro.* (I hope you came by metro.)
• Contrast: *Dudo que lo hagan hoy* (future action) vs. *Dudo que lo hayan hecho ya* (completed action).

items.spanish: Me alegro de que estés aquí (ahora) y me alegro de que hayas venido (pasado).
items.english: I'm glad you're here (now) and I'm glad you came (past).

items.spanish: ¿Crees que llueva esta tarde? vs. ¿Crees que haya llovido anoche?
items.english: Do you think it will rain this afternoon? vs. Do you think it rained last night?

items.spanish: Es una lástima que no puedan venir mañana vs. que no hayan podido venir ayer.
items.english: It's a pity they can't come tomorrow vs. that they couldn't come yesterday.

sections.content: Ask yourself: Is the action finished relative to now? If yes, use *haya + participio*.
